dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: SHARDFALL

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: Do you know how long it takes to seal a berth after its pressure plate fails?

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Depends on whether your crew uses the repair schedule or tries to finish it with a wrench and a prayer.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: Two nights. My crew slept in suits. We sent our replacement plates to Auric because you said the shelter roof would go before morning. The roof is still there. Our berth is leaking.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: I heard.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: You heard. You didn't come.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: I sent a team.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: A mechanic with one borrowed welder. The repair lasted until the first pressure cycle. I don't think that's a team.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: No. It's not.

panelPlan: SHARDFALL. The captains' chamber is filling for an ordinary dispute about repair allocations. The witnesses expected an accounting argument. Oren Pike has.
The accusation catches her off balance. Abby, standing to one side, watches the two captains rather than the gathering spectators.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *SHARDFALL. The captains' chamber is filling for an ordinary dispute about repair allocations. The witnesses expected an accounting argument. Oren Pike has brought the accounting. Two pressure plates lie on the table, one bent from load and one new enough to show where it came from.*
*The accusation catches her off balance. Abby, standing to one side, watches the two captains rather than the gathering spectators.*

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: You gave away supplies I earned, then sent me an apology that couldn't hold air. I want that entered into the record.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: Then enter it. The plate transfer was recorded. Nobody's asking your crew to pretend the loss didn't happen.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: I want her standing reviewed, not just the invoice.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: Because she made a decision you disagreed with?

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: Because she decided how much of my crew's safety she was entitled to spend. If that's what leadership means now, I want to know when we voted for it.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: You patched it twice.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: Of course we did. What did you think we'd do, go to sleep and let the berth empty?

panelPlan: Tess has been looking at the warped plate. She notices a repaired edge the witness hasn't mentioned.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Tess has been looking at the warped plate. She notices a repaired edge the witness hasn't mentioned.*

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: I thought you'd get the replacement before it reached that point.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: That's the thing about knowing everyone else's needs. Sometimes you miss the ones under your nose.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: The Auric roof would have collapsed. I won't apologize for keeping those people breathing.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: I'm not asking you to. I'm asking whether you'd have done it if your crew had to sleep in pressure suits instead of mine.

panelPlan: She nods. It's more painful than the public challenge, because he is right about that much.
She opens her mouth, then shuts it. Pike sees the hesitation and makes his formal challenge before the witnesses. Abby starts forward, but Tess raises a hand.

*She opens her mouth, then shuts it. Pike sees the hesitation and makes his formal challenge before the witnesses. Abby starts forward, but Tess raises a hand: the challenge is lawful, and she will answer it herself.*

summary: A FIGHT PEOPLE CAN AFFORD TO WATCH (P02–P03) — 1/3

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: VEIL MARKET

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: The greatest trick in politics. Offer a fight to a hungry audience and they forget they haven't eaten.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: I don't think they've forgotten. The woman at the front has been asking for her allotment since I got here.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Six pallets diverted. Who authorized it?

dialogueInline.speaker: ATTENDANT
dialogueInline.text: I have the release marks. One signature is from yesterday. One isn't in the roster anymore.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Then why were the pallets allowed out?

dialogueInline.speaker: ATTENDANT
dialogueInline.text: Because people shouted at me from both ends of the hall and I had to decide whether the children at the door got fed before I found a supervisor.

Naomi is about to argue. Then she sees the tired attendant's shaking hands.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: All right. Show me the release marks. We'll find which pallet can come back today. The children aren't waiting for us to decide whose fault this was.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I'll trace the buyers. If the pallets went to a legitimate shelter, we don't seize them back and call it accounting.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Agreed. I'm glad we established that before somebody tried to improve the problem with a weapon.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: We can move the patrol behind Broken Oath while the arena holds everyone's attention.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: You'd put an armed cruiser behind a Shard vessel while its captain is on a duel floor? I'm struggling to see how that could be misunderstood.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: We would gain a defensible approach.

panelPlan: THUNDERBREAK. Venn and Deka hear the duel mentioned during a route briefing. An officer wants to reposition Fleet vessels while the captains are occupied.

summary: A FIGHT PEOPLE CAN AFFORD TO WATCH (P02–P03) — 3/3

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: We would also turn a political challenge into an excuse for Fleet maneuvering. What transit operation requires that approach?

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: None at present.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Then no. What does require our attention?

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: An unarmed repair tug needs a safe crossing, and the same dispute that's keeping their captain in Shardfall means no one has cleared the berth allocation. I'd be glad to spend our time on something with a real arrival time.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: SHARDFALL — DUEL CHAMBER

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: I told them not to let you bring anything onto the floor.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: If I meant to kill you with a radiator fitting, I wouldn't advertise it.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: It's a theatrical gesture.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Coming from you, that's a remarkably sensitive accusation.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: We lost the cooling margin that would have let Gravefire take another paid run. My crew is eating from repaired stores. I was wrong not to ask what giving up those pressure plates would mean for your people. I wasn't the only one who paid.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: The difference is that you decided to pay. My crew didn't.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: You're right.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: And if I'd refused them?

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: I might have taken them anyway.

panelPlan: Tess enters the duel chamber before the witnesses return. Pike is inspecting his weapon and adjusting a grip. She carries the damaged fitting from Gravefire's.
He does not smile. She sees it and becomes serious.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Tess enters the duel chamber before the witnesses return. Pike is inspecting his weapon and adjusting a grip. She carries the damaged fitting from Gravefire's radiator, a part her engineers have been unable to replace. She lays it beside his plates.*
*He does not smile. She sees it and becomes serious.*

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: There. That's the answer I came for.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: It shouldn't be enough. Not for a captain. What happened to those families under that roof mattered. What happened to your crew matters. You can demand an accounting for both.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: You talk as though there's some perfect answer that would keep everyone alive and every ship repaired.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: No. I've been trying to tell you there isn't.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: I'm a good captain, Tess.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: I know that.

panelPlan: He looks at the two pieces of damaged metal on the table.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *He looks at the two pieces of damaged metal on the table.*

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: People talk about me as though I pose for a camera while other people work. My crew survived a failed supply season because I kept that ship running when the Triarch couldn't be bothered to send us anything. The men and women in that berth trust me. I don't want to be the captain who lets people take their safety while I smile and accept a compliment for being generous.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Then let's not make them watch us pretend this is a simple question.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: They're already watching.

panelPlan: For the first time she hears more than the political demand. She puts her fitting back in her pocket.
The witnesses return. Pike readies his weapon. Tess removes her outer jacket and hands it to the attendant with unusual care; the garment is repaired in too.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: VEIL MARKET

dialogueInline.speaker: WORKER
dialogueInline.text: I told them to form a line. They're not listening.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Because a line doesn't guarantee food. Open the other service door.

dialogueInline.speaker: WORKER
dialogueInline.text: The mechanism is jammed. The lock hasn't been touched since the last ration change.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Does it open from the inside?

dialogueInline.speaker: WORKER
dialogueInline.text: Yes, if you can get the pressure catch loose.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Then get me two people who know the mechanism and half my unloading crew. The freighters can wait.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: If you divert that many crew, the second relief load doesn't finish unloading until morning.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Then it doesn't. That man is going to be crushed long before morning.

sourceActionBeats: *At Veil Market, a crush has formed at the only open ration door. The missing six pallets have meant smaller portions, and people have decided the only way to get enough is to reach the counter first. An elderly man has fallen against the shutter.*

*Jex hesitates, then joins the workers rather than continuing to argue. The catch gives way with a metallic screech. The second door opens onto a narrow corridor that must be cleared before people can move. Naomi refuses to let the crowd rush it.*

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: You at the front, yes, you. I need you to take the next ten people slowly. If you run, the door closes again. Everybody behind them waits until they have space.

dialogueInline.speaker: WOMAN
dialogueInline.text: And if we get there and there's nothing left?

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: There may not be enough for full allotments tonight. But there's an open door, and no one gets any food if we trample each other. Can you help me get the first ten through?

The woman takes a breath, takes the elderly man's arm, and begins moving the group. The crowd is angry. It does not become grateful all at once. But the crush.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: SHARDFALL DUEL FLOOR

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: You should have listened when I asked for those plates.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: I'm listening now. I'd be grateful if you stopped talking while I do it.

dialogueInline.speaker: WITNESS
dialogueInline.text: Captain Pike yields. The challenge is concluded.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: You could finish it. No one here would stop you.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: I don't want to kill you.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: You think that makes you better than me?

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: No. I think it means my sister can stop making that face and somebody can put a bandage on my arm.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: My crew still has a leaking berth.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: I know.

panelPlan: SHARDFALL DUEL FLOOR. Pike fights like a veteran. His first exchanges are cautious, probing Tess's damaged balance and her tendency to favor her stronger side..
Pike comes in again. The cut forces her to change her guard. She recognizes that he expects an immediate counter from her injured side, and she lets.
Abby realizes she has been grimacing. She doesn't apologize. Tess steps away and accepts the bandage, allowing the medic to examine the cut rather than waving.

sourceActionBeats: *SHARDFALL DUEL FLOOR. Pike fights like a veteran. His first exchanges are cautious, probing Tess's damaged balance and her tendency to favor her stronger side. Tess makes the mistake of assuming his carefully staged public posture means he is less dangerous than he is. He cuts her left forearm.*

*The cut is clean and bad enough to make her fingers hesitate when she tries to tighten her grip. No one cheers. Abby involuntarily steps forward before catching herself; she has to watch the lawful challenge as a sister, not interfere as a captain.*

*Pike comes in again. The cut forces her to change her guard. She recognizes that he expects an immediate counter from her injured side, and she lets him believe he's created an opening. When he commits his weight too far, she pivots, catches his wrist with her good arm and forces the weapon down. It skitters across the floor. Tess holds his arm until the witness declares the lawful yield.*
*Pike looks at her, breathless and furious. Tess's sleeve is darkening. Several spectators wait for a final punishment or a political statement.*
*Abby realizes she has been grimacing. She doesn't apologize. Tess steps away and accepts the bandage, allowing the medic to examine the cut rather than waving away the risk.*

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: Winning this doesn't fix it.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: I know that too.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: I'll submit the replacement request again. In the morning.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: You should. I'll confirm the original transfer was my decision.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: You could have told me how much that cut hurt.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: I was trying not to encourage him.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: I'm serious.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: So am I. Give me the sleeve. No, not that way, you'll pull it over the wound.

He leaves without thanks. His witnesses record the result. Tess is still bleeding. Abby comes closer, carrying her jacket.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: SHARDFALL — CAPTAINS / VEIL MARKET

dialogueInline.speaker: RAID MASK
dialogueInline.text: Confederacy berths are assigned for Confederacy service. Your vessels have declined that service.

dialogueInline.speaker: FIRST CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: We still have repair commitments and crew aboard. Those berths were paid for.

dialogueInline.speaker: RAID MASK
dialogueInline.text: The berths are frozen pending review.

dialogueInline.speaker: SECOND CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: Your review will outlast our stores.

dialogueInline.speaker: RAID MASK
dialogueInline.text: You made your choice.

dialogueInline.speaker: FIRST CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: Don't tell them we belong to you now. We don't.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: I wasn't going to.

dialogueInline.speaker: FIRST CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: Everybody's going to say that's why we refused. That we've signed up to take your orders.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: I can't stop what they'll say. I can ask where you need to put your ships.

panelPlan: Veil Market is still hungry when the duel's result reaches it. At Shardfall, two captains who had hesitated now refuse Raid's muster. They do not announce.
The first captain looks toward Abby, who has been standing at the back.

One speaks of the medical convoys; the other of the way refusal was punished. Neither is certain where their crews will sleep.*
*The first captain looks toward Abby, who has been standing at the back.*

dialogueInline.speaker: SECOND CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: We're already doing the arithmetic. There isn't space for both. Even if someone takes us, the crews will need to work off the fuel and docking charges.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: Then show me the figures. I'll ask the captains who have space, and I'll tell you who can actually take you rather than make promises to both.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: They'll accept our protection. We could make it conditional on bringing them under Fleet command.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: It would be easy, while they're desperate.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Yes. That's the trouble. Offer safe transit on request. Not a commission. Not a contract to surrender their ships.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: We may never have leverage this good again.

panelPlan: On Thunderbreak, an officer proposes offering Fleet berths contingent on enlistment under the Fleet defensive chain.
Venn considers the word rather than merely dismissing the officer.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.

*Venn considers the word rather than merely dismissing the officer.*

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: You're probably right. We should be careful what we become when we discover we have it.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: I'll log safe passage for any ship that requests it. No change to command. Their hulls stay theirs.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: You didn't need me for that.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: No. You were the useful witness.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I'll try to remain useful.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: SHARDFALL / VEIL MARKET

dialogueInline.speaker: CHILD
dialogueInline.text: It was open yesterday.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: A lot of things were open yesterday.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: I'm not going to bleed on your floor. That was my sister's concern too.

dialogueInline.speaker: CHILD
dialogueInline.text: Did the other captain hurt you?

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Yes. I hurt him as well. Neither of us was improved by it.

dialogueInline.speaker: CHILD
dialogueInline.text: Then why did you do it?

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: We disagreed about something that mattered to both of us. We picked a bad way of proving which of us could win a fight. It didn't settle the thing we disagreed about.

dialogueInline.speaker: CHILD
dialogueInline.text: That's stupid.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: I'm finding it difficult to argue with you.
